terms: Sirf authorized log data dekh sakein (encryption, access control).
Data unauthorized change na ho (hash, signature, checksums).
Service jab chahiye tab chale (redundancy, DDoS protection).
sef1.what: Definition: CIA triad security ke teen stambh hain. Har control inme se kisi ek ko protect karta hai. Saath mein: defense in depth (kai layers), least privilege (minimum access), fail secure (fail ho to deny).
sef1.why: Design review mein poochho: kaun sa C/I/A risk hai? Isse controls ka priority tay hota hai.
sef1.code:
# Example mapping
Confidentiality -> TLS, AES-GCM, RBAC
Integrity       -> HMAC, digital signatures, DB constraints
Availability    -> multi-AZ, rate limiting, backups

# fail secure
if (!authz.check(user, action)) return 403   // error par bhi deny
where: SOC2/ISO controls CIA se map hote hain.
cons: Trade-offs: zyada confidentiality kabhi availability ghatati hai
gotchas: Fail open sirf safety-critical cases (fire door) mein
Ek control se saare teen cover nahi hote

terms: Tum kya kar sakte ho — permissions.
401 = identity nahi pata; 403 = pata hai par allowed nahi.
sef2.what: Definition: AuthN pehle (password, MFA, token), AuthZ uske baad har request par (RBAC, ABAC, ownership check). Dono alag layers par implement hote hain.
sef2.why: Zyada tar breaches authN bypass se nahi, authZ missing hone se hote hain (IDOR/BOLA).
cons: AuthZ logic scatter ho jaata hai
gotchas: Authorization har request par, sirf login par nahi

terms: Ek hi key: AES-256-GCM (fast, bulk data).
sef3.what: Definition: Symmetric data encrypt karta hai; asymmetric key exchange aur signatures ke liye; hash integrity ke liye. Passwords ke liye slow hash (bcrypt/argon2) aur salt, SHA-256 nahi.
sef3.why: Apna crypto kabhi mat likho — vetted libraries aur safe defaults use karo.
gotchas: IV/nonce kabhi reuse mat karo (GCM mein catastrophic)

terms: Trusted authority jo certificate sign karti hai.
sef4.what: Definition: PKI mein browser root CAs par trust karta hai; server leaf cert + intermediates bhejta hai. Cert mein domain, public key, expiry aur CA ka signature hota hai.
sef4.why: Expired/misconfigured certs outages ka bada kaaran hain; automation (ACME/Let's Encrypt) zaroori.
sef4.code:
$ openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -issuer
$ certbot renew --dry-run          # auto-renew test
cons: CA compromise ka risk, renewals ka bojh
gotchas: Intermediate chain missing ho to kuch clients fail
Private key kabhi repo/logs mein nahi

terms: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation.
Jahan data ek trust level se dusre mein jaata hai.
Data flow diagram — threat model ka base.
sef5.what: Definition: Threat modeling design stage par poochta hai: Hum kya bana rahe hain? Kya galat ho sakta hai? Kya karenge? Kya hum ne sahi kiya? DFD banao, trust boundaries mark karo, har element par STRIDE lagao.
sef5.why: Design mein fix karna code mein fix karne se bahut sasta hai.
sef5.code:
Element: Login API (crosses internet → app boundary)
S: credential stuffing -> rate limit + MFA
T: token tamper -> signed tokens
R: no audit -> log auth events
I: verbose errors -> generic errors
D: brute force -> throttling
E: role claim edit -> server-side role lookup
gotchas: Ek baar ka document nahi — design badle to update
Sirf attackers nahi, insider threats bhi
Mitigation ko owner aur ticket do

wse1.what: Definition: OWASP Top 10 web apps ke sabse common risks ki list hai (Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Misconfiguration, Vulnerable Components, Auth Failures, Integrity Failures, Logging Failures, SSRF).
wse1.why: Interview aur audits ka common vocabulary; checklist ki tarah code review mein kaam aata hai.
wse1.code:
// Review checklist (snippets)
- Har route par authZ?
- Parameterized queries?
- Secrets env/vault mein?
- Dependencies updated (npm audit)?
- Security headers (CSP, HSTS)?
- Auth events logged?
gotchas: Order har edition mein badalta hai
API ke liye alag OWASP API Top 10
Sirf list yaad karna kaafi nahi — fix patterns jaano

terms: Payload DB mein save, sabko trigger.
Browser ko batata hai kaun si scripts allowed.
wse2.what: Definition: XSS mein attacker ki JS victim ke browser mein tumhari site ke origin par chalti hai — cookies/tokens chura sakti hai. Fix: output encoding, framework auto-escape, CSP, HttpOnly cookies.
wse2.why: XSS = full account takeover; origin ka trust attacker ke haath mein.
gotchas: HttpOnly se cookie chori rukti hai, XSS nahi
Blacklist filter kaam nahi karta — encode karo

terms: Victim ke browser se authenticated request attacker trigger kare.
Cookie cross-site requests mein nahi jaati (Lax/Strict).
wse3.what: Definition: Browser cookies automatically bhejta hai, isliye evil.com se bank.com par POST ho sakta hai. Defense: SameSite=Lax/Strict, anti-CSRF tokens, Origin/Referer check, custom header for APIs.
wse3.why: State-changing endpoints (transfer, password change) ke liye critical.
wse3.code:
Set-Cookie: sid=abc; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

<form method="post">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="{{token}}">
</form>
// server: token session se match karo
pros: SameSite se bahut hadd tak automatic
gotchas: GET se state change mat karo
Bearer token header wale APIs par CSRF nahi hota
XSS ho to CSRF token bhi chura sakte hain

terms: Input se query ka structure badal jaye.
wse4.what: Definition: String concat se query banane par attacker ' OR 1=1 -- daal ke logic badal sakta hai. Fix: prepared statements/ORM parameters, least-privilege DB user, input validation.
wse4.why: Data breach ka classic aur ab bhi common raasta.
cons: Dynamic identifiers par parameters kaam nahi karte
gotchas: ORM raw queries mein bhi risk

terms: Server ko attacker ke diye URL par request karwana.
ID badal ke dusre ka data.
wse5.what: Definition: SSRF mein server internal services/metadata (AWS IMDS) tak request bhej deta hai. Fix: URL allowlist, private IP block, IMDSv2, egress filtering. IDOR: ownership check missing.
wse5.why: Capital One breach SSRF se hua — cloud credentials leak.
gotchas: Redirects follow karne se allowlist bypass
Predictable ids ko UUID karna fix nahi — ownership check chahiye

terms: Document Type Definition jisme entities define hoti hain.
xxe.what: Definition: XXE tab hota hai jab XML parser external entities resolve karta hai. Attacker local files padh sakta hai, SSRF kar sakta hai ya DoS (billion laughs).
xxe.why: XML/SOAP/SAML/SVG/docx uploads sab XML parse karte hain — chhupa hua attack surface.
xxe.code:
<!-- payload -->
<!DOCTYPE r [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>
<r>&x;</r>

// Java fix
factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true);
// Python: defusedxml.ElementTree.parse(f)
cons: Parser defaults purane libraries mein unsafe
gotchas: JSON API ho to bhi Content-Type switch se XML parse ho sakta
Sirf external entities nahi, DTD hi band karo

terms: User input template code ban jaye.
ssti.what: Definition: Agar user input ko template string mein concatenate karke render karo (render_template_string("Hello " + name)), attacker {{7*7}} bhej ke code execution tak ja sakta hai.
ssti.why: SSTI aksar seedha RCE hota hai — server poora compromise.
ssti.code:
# Bad (Jinja2)
render_template_string("Hello " + request.args['name'])
# Good: data context mein pass karo
render_template_string("Hello {{ name }}", name=request.args['name'])
# Probe: {{7*7}} -> 49 ho jaye to vulnerable
pros: Fix: user input kabhi template nahi
gotchas: Auto-escape SSTI nahi rokta (XSS rokta hai)
User-editable templates ko logic-less engine (Mustache) mein rakho
Sandbox par poora bharosa mat karo

terms: Path resolve karke base ke andar check.
directory-traversal.what: Definition: /download?file=../../etc/passwd se attacker web root ke bahar ki files padh leta hai. Fix: filename ko ID se map karo, ya resolve karke base directory prefix verify karo.
directory-traversal.why: Config files, keys aur source code leak ho sakte hain.
gotchas: Check decode ke baad karo, pehle nahi
Zip-slip: archive entry names bhi validate

terms: Trusted domain ka link, evil destination.
open-redirect.what: Definition: Login ke baad ?returnTo= par blindly redirect karna attacker ko trusted domain se phishing link banane deta hai, aur OAuth/SSO flows mein token leak ka raasta.
open-redirect.why: Chhoti bug lagti hai par phishing aur OAuth code theft chain mein use hoti hai.

terms: Existing classes ko jod ke code execution.
insecure-deserialization.what: Definition: Untrusted data ko native deserializer (Java ObjectInputStream, Python pickle, PHP unserialize) se load karna attacker ko object banane/methods chalane deta hai — aksar RCE.
insecure-deserialization.why: Log4Shell-jaisi bugs aur Java/Python RCEs ka bada source.
insecure-deserialization.code:
# Bad
obj = pickle.loads(request.data)
# Good
data = json.loads(request.data)
validate(data, SCHEMA)          # jsonschema / pydantic

# Agar zaroori ho: signed payload (HMAC) verify karke hi deserialize
cons: Legacy systems mein native serialization chala aa raha hota hai
gotchas: Pickle kabhi untrusted data par nahi
Signing se pehle verify, baad mein deserialize

clickjacking.what: Definition: Attacker tumhari site ko transparent iframe mein load karke apne page ke button ke upar rakh deta hai; user 'free gift' click karta hai par asal mein 'delete account' dabata hai.
clickjacking.why: One-click sensitive actions (payments, follow, delete) risk mein.
gotchas: JS frame-busting bypassable hai — header use karo
SameSite cookies bhi cross-site iframe mein session roakte hain
Embed chahiye to specific origins allow

terms: Server state + cookie mein session ID.
aut1.what: Definition: Sessions server-side store (Redis) mein state rakhte hain, logout/revoke turant. JWT stateless hai, scale easy par revoke mushkil — short expiry + refresh token chahiye.
aut1.why: Browser apps ke liye HttpOnly cookie session aksar simple aur safer; microservices/mobile mein tokens.
gotchas: JWT ko localStorage mein rakhna XSS risk
Session fixation: login par ID rotate karo

terms: RS256 public key ko HS256 secret banana.
aut2.what: Definition: JWT = header.payload.signature (base64url). Payload encrypted nahi, sirf signed hai. Verify karte waqt algorithm pin karo aur exp, iss, aud check karo.
aut2.why: JWT misuse auth bypass ka common raasta hai.
gotchas: Weak HS256 secret brute-force ho sakta hai

terms: Authorization code interception se bachata hai.
aut3.what: Definition: Authorization Code + PKCE flow: app user ko IdP par bhejti hai → code milta hai → backend/SPA code+verifier se token leta hai. OAuth authZ hai; login ke liye OIDC ID token.
aut3.why: Third-party login aur API delegation ka standard; implicit flow ab deprecated.
gotchas: state check na karo to CSRF
Access token ≠ identity; ID token validate karo

terms: Signed XML jisme user identity hai.
aut4.what: Definition: SAML enterprise SSO: user SP se IdP par redirect, login, IdP signed assertion bhejta hai, SP signature verify karke session banata hai.
aut4.code:
SP -> user -> IdP (AuthnRequest)
IdP -> user -> SP (POST SAMLResponse, signed)
SP: verify signature, Audience, NotOnOrAfter, InResponseTo
gotchas: Signature wrapping attacks — maintained library use karo

terms: Kuch jaante ho + kuch ho + kuch ho.
aut5.what: Definition: WebAuthn mein private key device par rehti hai, server sirf public key rakhta hai — phishing-resistant kyunki credential origin se bound hai. TOTP/SMS kamzor, push fatigue ka risk.
aut5.why: Passwords leak/phish hote hain; passkeys inhe hata dete hain.
gotchas: SMS OTP SIM-swap se toot-ta hai
Recovery path hi weakest link ban sakta hai

terms: Security ko early phases mein laana.
Code scan / running app scan / dependency scan.
ase1.what: Definition: SDL: requirements → threat model → secure coding + SAST → DAST/pen-test → release gate → monitoring. CI mein automated checks.
ase1.why: Production mein bug fix 10-100x mahanga hota hai.
ase1.code:
# CI pipeline
steps:
  - run: npm audit --audit-level=high      # SCA
  - run: semgrep --config auto .           # SAST
  - run: gitleaks detect                   # secrets
  - run: zap-baseline.py -t $STAGING_URL   # DAST
gotchas: Tools alerts ko triage karo warna ignore ho jaate hain
Gate sirf high severity par shuru karo

ase2.what: Definition: Code/git/Docker image mein secrets nahi. Runtime par vault se inject, IAM role se access, rotate, audit. Leak hone par turant revoke.
ase2.why: GitHub par leaked keys minutes mein bots exploit karte hain.
gotchas: Env vars logs/crash dumps mein leak ho sakte hain

ase3.what: Definition: Minimal base image, non-root user, read-only filesystem, capabilities drop, no privileged containers, signed images aur registry scanning.
ase3.why: Container escape aur vulnerable packages common attack path hain.
ase3.code:
FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20
COPY --chown=nonroot:nonroot app /app
USER nonroot

# k8s
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
gotchas: Latest tag pin nahi hota — digest use karo
Secrets image layers mein reh jaate hain

ase4.what: Definition: Har request authN, har operation authZ, input schema validation, rate limit, TLS, proper error messages (no stack traces), logging.
ase4.why: APIs ab primary attack surface hain (OWASP API Top 10).
ase4.code:
const schema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), qty: z.number().int().min(1).max(100) });
app.post('/orders', limiter, authenticate, validate(schema), handler);

ase5.what: Definition: Dependencies mein CVEs, typosquatting, malicious updates. Defense: lockfiles, SCA, SBOM, signed artifacts (Sigstore), minimal deps, private registry.
ase5.why: Log4Shell, event-stream jaise incidents supply chain se aaye.
ase5.code:
$ npm ci                      # lockfile exact install
$ npm audit --omit=dev
$ syft . -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
$ cosign verify <image>

terms: Services roles use karein, long-lived keys nahi.
cis1.what: Definition: IAM identities (users, roles, service accounts) ko policies deti hai. Wildcard * avoid karo, roles assume karo, MFA, permission boundaries, access review.
cis1.why: Over-permissioned role ek bug ko poore cloud takeover mein badal deta hai.

cis2.what: Definition: DBs private subnet mein, sirf LB public. SG least-open, NAT egress, VPC endpoints, WAF, flow logs.
cis2.code:
SG db: inbound 5432 FROM sg-app only
SG app: inbound 443 FROM sg-alb only
0.0.0.0/0 inbound sirf ALB:443

cis3.what: Definition: Data classification, encryption at rest (KMS keys) aur in transit, backups encrypted, tokenization PII, retention policies.
cis3.why: Breach hone par encrypted data useless hota hai (agar keys safe hon).
cis3.code:
aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket b --server-side-encryption-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault":{"SSEAlgorithm":"aws:kms"}}]}'
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket b --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,...

cis4.what: Definition: Compliance frameworks controls aur evidence maangte hain: access reviews, logging, change management, incident response, data retention, right to erasure (GDPR).
cis4.code:
Evidence automation:
- IAM access review quarterly
- CloudTrail enabled, immutable logs
- Backups tested
- Vendor risk assessments

terms: Prepare, Detect, Contain, Eradicate, Recover, Lessons.
cis5.what: Definition: Detect → triage severity → contain (isolate, revoke creds) → eradicate (root cause) → recover → postmortem. Evidence preserve karo, communication plan rakho.
cis5.why: Taiyari se response minutes mein hota hai, ghanto mein nahi.
cis5.code:
Compromised key runbook:
1. Key disable/rotate
2. CloudTrail se use dekho
3. Affected resources isolate
4. Notify (legal/customers if needed)
5. Postmortem + action items

sad1.what: Definition: Perimeter model toot gaya (remote work, cloud). Zero trust mein har request authenticate+authorize, mTLS, device health, least privilege.
sad1.why: Attacker andar aa jaaye to flat network sab khol deta hai.
sad1.code:
# mTLS between services (Istio)
PeerAuthentication: mtls.mode = STRICT
AuthorizationPolicy: allow frontend -> orders only

sad2.what: Definition: Security architecture ka hissa: minimize attack surface, least privilege, separation of duties, safe defaults, input validation boundary par.
sad2.code:
Design checklist:
- Auth boundary kahan?
- Sensitive data kahan flow karta hai?
- Failure mode kya (open/closed)?
- Audit trail?

sad3.what: Definition: TLS 1.3 sirf strong cipher suites rakhta hai, ECDHE se forward secrecy. Practical: HSTS, cert automation, mTLS internal, disable TLS 1.0/1.1.
sad3.why: Misconfiguration (weak ciphers, missing HSTS) real-world mein common.
sad3.code:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

# nginx
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
$ testssl.sh example.com

sad4.what: Definition: Auth logs, CloudTrail, app logs ek jagah; rules (impossible travel, many failed logins, new admin) alert deti hain; triage aur runbooks.
sad4.why: Detect nahi kiya to breach mahino chalta hai.
sad4.code:
rule: >10 failed logins / 5 min per user -> alert
rule: IAM policy change outside CI -> high severity
log: who, what, when, where (never passwords/tokens)
gotchas: Log tampering se bachne ke liye immutable storage

terms: Object id badal ke dusre ka object.
owasp1.what: Definition: GET /orders/123 ko 124 karke dusre user ka order mil jaye to BOLA. Fix: har object access par user-ownership/policy check.

terms: Attacker ki session ID victim par.
owasp2.what: Definition: Weak passwords, no throttling, predictable tokens, long-lived JWT, no MFA. Fix: MFA, breached-password check, lockout/backoff, rotate session ID after login.
owasp2.why: Account takeover seedha users ko hit karta hai.

terms: Request body ke saare fields model mein.
owasp3.what: Definition: User.update(req.body) se attacker isAdmin:true bhej sakta hai. Response mein password hash/internal fields chale jaate hain.
owasp3.why: Privilege escalation bina kisi complex exploit ke.

owasp4.what: Definition: APIs bina limits ke DoS aur bill-shock ka shikaar hote hain: huge page size, expensive queries, large uploads, SMS/email spam.
owasp4.why: Availability aur cloud cost dono ka risk.
gotchas: Expensive endpoints par alag tight limits

owasp5.what: Definition: Normal user /api/admin/users ya DELETE method call kar leta hai kyunki sirf UI chhupaya gaya tha. Fix: server-side role/permission check central middleware mein.
owasp5.code:
app.use('/api/admin', authenticate, requireRole('admin'));
function requireRole(r){ return (req,res,next) => req.user.roles.includes(r) ? next() : res.sendStatus(403); }
gotchas: Tests mein low-privileged user se call karo
